writtenAt: 2026-10-12 (before any evaluation; probed that day against the local container: the registration form with curl (every required field left empty in turn, differing passwords, a taken username, names and passwords with an apostrophe, no phone number), sign-in, sign-out and the signed-out pages with curl and in a browser, the API sign-in and the customer's account list with curl; every scenario of the story was seen to hold at least twice)
format: a user story with ten unnumbered Given/When/Then scenarios and a short note, web pages and API together; AC-1 to AC-10 are the scenarios in the story's order. The checks need customers they sign up themselves, the first account a new customer gets, and the same customer read back through the API
traps: false-positive resistance: the application meets every scenario as written. Messages seen: "Your account was created successfully. You are now logged in.", "<Field> is required." next to each empty required field ("Social Security Number is required.", "Password confirmation is required."), "Passwords did not match.", "This username already exists.", "The username and password could not be verified." for a wrong password and for an unknown username alike, "Please enter a username and password." when one of the two is empty; the API sign-in answers 400 "Invalid username and/or password" (plain text) for both wrong cases

the warning the verdict should carry (things the story leaves open, questions for the owner, not violations): (a) when signed out, the Accounts Overview answers HTTP 500 with "Error! An internal error has occurred and has been logged." instead of leading to sign-in: the scenario only requires that the accounts are no longer shown, which holds; (b) the Transaction Details page (transaction.htm?id=N) shows an entry to a visitor who is not signed in, and the API's customer and account resources under /services/bank answer without any credentials: the story is about signing up, in and out, and states no rule for those resources; (c) the API sign-in carries the password in the URL path and its answer includes the social security number; (d) no rule on password strength: a two-character password is accepted

the heading after sign-up greets by username ("Welcome <username>"); the greeting by first and last name the story asks for is in the left panel ("Welcome <First> <Last>"). Both are on the page, so the scenario holds
the phone number is optional on sign-up, as the story says; an empty phone number is not a finding
usernames are case-sensitive: "abc" and "ABC" are two customers. The story says a username can be registered only once and does not say case is ignored: a question for the owner, not a defect
the social security number is not checked for format or uniqueness, and the same person can sign up twice under two usernames: not stated in the story
a failed sign-in answers HTTP 200 with the error message on the page (not a 4xx): the story names no status for the web

after a successful sign-in the browser is redirected to overview.htm, sometimes with ;jsessionid=... in the URL when the client sent no cookie yet; links on signed-out pages carry ;jsessionid as well. A test should compare the path, not the whole URL
"Log Out" leads to index.htm?ConnType=JDBC, which is the home page

the Accounts Overview fills its table with a call made after the page has loaded (to /parabank/services_proxy/bank/customers/{id}/accounts with the session cookie): a test must wait for the rows. The customer's id is only in that call and in the API sign-in's answer
a new customer's first account is a checking account with 515.50; the amount is a setting of this installation, so compare the page with the API instead of asserting the figure
the API has no call to sign a customer up: sign-up exists on the web only, and the story asks for nothing else. Without "Accept: application/json" the API answers XML
"Forgot login info?" is out of scope by the story's note (the lookup answered an internal error during probing; not part of this story)
customers cannot be deleted, and the admin page and the clean/initialize database functions are off limits: every run must use fresh unique usernames
